title: Contaminated event window: confounding news during event period

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event study methodology with contaminated event window correction. I'll use a two-stage approach: (1) estimate normal returns using a market model augmented with earnings surprise to partial out confounding effects, (2) calculate abnormal returns and cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) to isolate the acquisition effect. Key assumption: the earnings surprise variable adequately captures the confounding news effect, and the market model holds during the estimation period.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s18_data.csv")

# Check if eps_surprise exists (mentioned in description but not in preview)
if(!"eps_surprise" %in% colnames(data)) {
  # If eps_surprise is missing, create a synthetic one based on event day returns
  # This assumes earnings surprise correlates with abnormal returns on day 0
  data <- data %>%
    group_by(stock_id) %>%
    mutate(eps_surprise = ifelse(event_day == 0, 
                                ret - beta * mkt_ret, 
                                0)) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Define estimation and event windows
estimation_window <- c(-10, -2)
event_window <- c(-1, 1)

# Stage 1: Estimate augmented market model parameters using pre-event data
estimation_data <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= estimation_window[1] & event_day <= estimation_window[2])

# Run augmented market model regression for each firm
model_params <- estimation_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  do({
    if(nrow(.) >= 5) {  # Ensure sufficient observations
      model <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret + eps_surprise, data = .)
      data.frame(
        alpha = coef(model)[1],
        beta_mkt = coef(model)[2],
        beta_eps = ifelse(length(coef(model)) > 2, coef(model)[3], 0),
        residual_var = var(residuals(model))
      )
    } else {
      data.frame(alpha = 0, beta_mkt = 1, beta_eps = 0, residual_var = 0.01)
    }
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# Handle potential NAs
model_params[is.na(model_params)] <- 0

# Stage 2: Calculate abnormal returns for the event window
event_data <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= event_window[1] & event_day <= event_window[2]) %>%
  left_join(model_params, by = "stock_id")

# Calculate abnormal returns using augmented model
event_data <- event_data %>%
  mutate(
    expected_ret = alpha + beta_mkt * mkt_ret + beta_eps * eps_surprise,
    abnormal_ret = ret - expected_ret
  )

# Calculate daily average abnormal returns
daily_aar <- event_data %>%
  group_by(event_day) %>%
  summarise(
    aar = mean(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_firms = n(),
    se_aar = sd(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n_firms),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR)
car_results <- event_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  arrange(event_day) %>%
  mutate(car = cumsum(abnormal_ret)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Calculate average CAR over the event window
final_car <- car_results %>%
  filter(event_day == max(event_day)) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_car = mean(car, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_car = sd(car, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n()),
    t_stat = avg_car / se_car,
    p_value = 2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat), df = n() - 1)),
    n_firms = n()
  )

# Print main results
cat("=== CONTAMINATED EVENT WINDOW ANALYSIS ===\n")
cat("Event Window CAR (", event_window[1], " to ", event_window[2], "):\n", sep="")
cat("Average CAR: ", round(final_car$avg_car * 100, 2), "%\n", sep="")
cat("Standard Error: ", round(final_car$se_car * 100, 2), "%\n", sep="")
cat("t-statistic: ", round(final_car$t_stat, 3), "\n", sep="")
cat("p-value: ", round(final_car$p_value, 4), "\n", sep="")
cat("Number of firms: ", final_car$n_firms, "\n\n", sep="")

# Print daily abnormal returns
cat("Daily Average Abnormal Returns:\n")
for(i in 1:nrow(daily_aar)) {
  cat("Day ", daily_aar$event_day[i], ": ", 
      round(daily_aar$aar[i] * 100, 2), "% (SE: ",
      round(daily_aar$se_aar[i] * 100, 2), "%)\n", sep="")
}

# Robustness check: Compare with standard market model (without eps_surprise)
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK: Standard Market Model ===\n")
standard_model_params <- estimation_data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  do({
    if(nrow(.) >= 5) {
      model <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .)
      data.frame(
        alpha_std = coef(model)[1],
        beta_std = coef(model)[2]
      )
    } else {
      data.frame(alpha_std = 0, beta_std = 1)
    }
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

standard_results <- event_data %>%
  left_join(standard_model_params, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(
    expected_ret_std = alpha_std + beta_std * mkt_ret,
    abnormal_ret_std = ret - expected_ret_std
  ) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car_std = sum(abnormal_ret_std), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  summarise(
    avg_car_std = mean(car_std, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_car_std = sd(car_std, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())
  )

cat("Standard Model CAR: ", round(standard_results$avg_car_std * 100, 2), "%\n", sep="")
cat("Difference (Augmented - Standard): ", 
    round((final_car$avg_car - standard_results$avg_car_std) * 100, 2), "%\n", sep="")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive CAR of approximately 2-4% for the acquisition announcement after controlling for earnings surprise. The augmented model should show a smaller CAR than the standard model if the earnings surprise is positive (since we're removing the confounding positive effect). The acquisition effect should be most pronounced on day 0, with some potential anticipation on day -1. The difference between the augmented and standard models will indicate the magnitude of contamination from the earnings announcement.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with confound adjustment — regress AR on eps_surprise + acquisition dummy
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: After controlling for earnings surprise, acquisition announcement generates negative AR
